## Executive Summary

Harbor & Pine's inventory platform, InvenTrack 6, was installed in 2011 and is now a constraint on growth. It cannot see stock across our 42 stores and two distribution centres in real time, which drives a 14.5% out-of-stock rate on our top 500 SKUs and roughly $3.4M in excess safety stock. This document assesses whether to replace it with a cloud inventory platform. Over three years the project is expected to deliver $4.83M in benefits against $2.74M in costs, a net benefit of $2.56M and an ROI of 93.4%, with payback within 14 months. There are a number of considerations, which are discussed below.

## Background

InvenTrack 6 runs on on-premise servers that reach end of vendor support in Q3 FY2025. Store replenishment is planned in spreadsheets, e.g. the weekly re-order file that Priya Raman's team rebuilds by hand every Monday. Counts are reconciled overnight, so the e-commerce site regularly sells items that are not on the shelf (approx. 1,900 cancelled online orders last quarter). Industry studies show that retailers who modernize their inventory systems cut stockouts by 30–50% and lift same-store sales by 5% or more.

A modern platform would allow us to leverage synergies across our omnichannel ecosystem and become a best-in-class operator. It would give buyers a single view of stock, automate re-ordering for roughly 80% of SKUs and let stores ship online orders from the shelf.

## Costs and Benefits

| Item | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 | 3-Year Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Software subscription | $420K | $420K | $420K | $1.26M |
| Implementation & integration | $1.2M | — | — | $1.2M |
| Training & change management | $180K | $60K | $40K | $280K |
| **Total costs** | **$1.8M** | **$480K** | **$460K** | **$2.74M** |
| Lower carrying cost of inventory | $350K | $900K | $1.1M | $2.35M |
| Recovered margin from fewer stockouts | $250K | $600K | $700K | $1.55M |
| Legacy maintenance avoided | $310K | $310K | $310K | $930K |
| **Total benefits** | **$910K** | **$1.81M** | **$2.11M** | **$4.83M** |

The ROI calculation is as follows. Net benefit = $4.83M − $2.74M = $2.56M, and ROI = $2.56M ÷ $2.74M = 93.4%. Cumulative cash flow turns positive in Year 2. The benefit ramp assumes carrying costs fall by 9.3% in Year 1 and 29.3% by Year 3 vs. today's baseline of $3.75M per year, i.e. roughly 2.3 fewer days of cover per store.

## Assumptions

- Go-live in all 42 stores by the end of Q3 FY2025, with the two distribution centres first.
- Subscription pricing is fixed at $420K per year for three years (vendor quote dated 12 March 2025).
- Gross margin on recovered sales is 38%.
- Benefits are not discounted; a 10% discount rate would reduce the net benefit by about $0.4M.
- The new system must be fast, user-friendly and integrate with all our existing systems.

## Risks

**Data migration.** Fourteen years of SKU history contain duplicates and retired codes; Tom Becker (IT Director) estimates 6–8 weeks of data cleansing before cut-over.

**Change fatigue.** Store teams are still adjusting to the new POS system rolled out in FY2024. Elena Sato (Head of Store Operations) has asked that training not overlap the holiday peak.

**Vendor lock-in.** A SaaS platform is very flexible, but we would give up control of the upgrade schedule and our data would sit in the vendor's cloud.

**Benefit realisation.** If the stockout reduction is half what we expect, Year 3 benefits fall to $1.76M and payback moves out by roughly six months.

Given these risks, and taking into account the end-of-support date, the cost of continued manual workarounds and the views of the steering group, it is our recommendation that Harbor & Pine approve the $1.2M implementation budget and the three-year subscription so that vendor selection can be finalised in Q2 and the project can begin.

## Next Steps

Best-in-class retailers move quickly on decisions like this. We propose a steering group review on 14 April and a decision by the end of April, so that the project team can be stood up in May and the first distribution centre can go live in Q3 FY2025.
